text:
I'll check that Claude Code is present and that the installed binary responds, then register the server.

```sh
claude --version
/usr/local/bin/tentmaker version --json
claude mcp add --scope user tentmaker -- /usr/local/bin/tentmaker mcp
claude mcp get tentmaker
```

I'm using the absolute path `/usr/local/bin/tentmaker` because the MCP server is launched by Claude Code, which may not have the same `PATH` as your shell. I'm also using `--scope user`, so the server is available in every project. Without it, `claude mcp add` registers the server only for the current directory.

Before I run these, I'd check with you on two things:

1. **Scope.** Do you want `user` (every project, my default here) or `local` (only this directory)?
2. **Write-access tools.** The MCP server runs as your user, not as root. The read tools (`status`, `pool`, `doctor`) will work. Tools that change the device will return an error saying they need root. If you want those tools available, I'd have to run the server under `sudo`, which I don't recommend registering with Claude Code. Use the CLI with `sudo` for changes instead.

If the scope is fine, I'll run the commands. Then I'll start a new Claude Code session and confirm that the `tentmaker` tools appear.
